subject: ventures/tender-bid-readiness
professional: a capture / bid manager for a small public-works contractor (Shipley- or APMP-trained) who runs the bid/no-bid gate; they check first that the tool recognises the solicitation's own vocabulary for the disqualifying items (FAR 52.228-1 'bid guarantee' / state 'bid security', FAR 'amendments' as well as 'addenda', 'preproposal conference', sealed-bid delivery, UK 'licence'), that the deadline it points to is the offer due date and not the question cut-off, that a negated requirement ('No bid bond is required') is not reported as a found requirement, and that the go/no-go guidance matches bid/no-bid practice (customer, competition, capability, Pwin, cost to bid as well as responsiveness).

evidence.correctness: check.mjs is seven case-insensitive regexes; each takes the FIRST match and returns up to 100 following characters as evidence; score = round(found/7*100). Recomputed by hand against FAR wording and common state/UK tender wording with node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/67bd57d3-d405-5f56-9673-f790b946bf15/scratchpad/tender/probe.mjs and node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/67bd57d3-d405-5f56-9673-f790b946bf15/scratchpad/tender/probe2.mjs (Node 22.23.4). Wrong outputs: (1) FAR 52.228-1 'Bid Guarantee ... shall be not less than 20 percent of the bid price' alone -> bond 'missed' (regex needs '(bid|tender|performance|payment) bond'); FAR 28.101-4 makes a missing bid guarantee generally nonresponsive, so this is the most disqualifying item; 'bid security ... certified check or surety bond' -> bond missed, the evidence instead lands under certification ('certified check'). (2) Questions line before the proposal line: 'Questions are due by 2 January 2027.\nProposals are due 20 January 2027 at 3pm.' -> deadline evidence 'due by 2 January 2027.' i.e. the question cut-off is shown under 'Find and verify the submission deadline'. (3) Negations count as found: 'No bid bond is required. No insurance certificate ... No site visit will be held. No license is required.' -> bond, insurance, certification, site-visit all Found, score 57. (4) Decoys: 'perform due diligence ... Payment is due net 30 ... email with any question about invoicing' -> deadline, submission, questions, certification, insurance Found, score 71 on text with no tender requirement. (5) The site-visit signal added in VENTURE.yaml's 2026-09-01 note misses FAR's own term: 'A preproposal conference will be held on 3 Dec. Attendance is mandatory.' -> missed; 'A mandatory site inspection' -> missed. (6) 'Offerors shall acknowledge receipt of all amendments' (FAR 52.214-3) -> questions missed; 'Gas Safe licence' (UK spelling, on a page about 'tenders') -> certification missed; 'Bids will be received until 2:00 PM' -> deadline missed; 'Sealed bids shall be delivered to Room 200' and 'returned via the e-tendering system' -> submission missed; 'named as additional insured ... $1,000,000 per occurrence' -> insurance missed. A FAR SF 1442-style construction excerpt scored 57% with insurance, licensing and submission missed. Correct where the exact keywords are present (test fixtures, 'closing date for tenders', 'Clarification questions by'). The arithmetic of the score is right (4/7 -> 57). Capped at 1: the outputs are wrong on the standard wording of the very items the tool exists to find.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features walked: paste and 'Check readiness' renders a per-signal Found/Not found list with action text and an evidence excerpt for found signals (index.html:48-51 render(), works); seven signals as the FAQ says (check.mjs:1-9, works); Clear button (works); local-only, no network calls (index.html has one module import of ./check.mjs, no fetch); usage counter with DNT/GPC and an opt-out checkbox whose state persists (index.html:29-49, present); guide page and GovWin comparison page served (curl https://marisstella.app/tender-bid-readiness/ 200, vs-govwin.html and should-i-bid-on-this-tender.html 307 -> 200 extensionless, LICENSE 200, served llms.txt rewritten to marisstella.app). Links to ../rfp-compliance-matrix/, ../tender-radar/, ../contractor-bid-readiness/ resolve to existing venture dirs. No TODOs or stubs. It does everything it lists; what it lists is small.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' from ventures/tender-bid-readiness: 16 pass, 0 fail (4 in check.test.mjs; the rest page/marketing assertions). Six seeded mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: removing 'closing date' (check.mjs:2) SURVIVED, dropping 'addend(um|a)' (check.mjs:8) SURVIVED, Math.round -> Math.floor in the score (check.mjs:20) SURVIVED, 'found < rules.length' -> '<=' so a 100% result says signals were missing (check.mjs:24) SURVIVED; removing 'bid|tender' from the bond rule (check.mjs:3) caught; removing bare 'insurance' (check.mjs:4) caught. 4 of 6 survived. No test covers a partial score, a negation, a FAR term, or which of two deadlines is reported.
evidence.craft: Read check.mjs (27 lines), check.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, vs-govwin.test.mjs, index.html, both content pages. Small, pure, dependency-free; escapeHtml applied to evidence before innerHTML (index.html:48-50), so pasted HTML is not injected. Defects: first-match-only extraction with no line or sentence boundary handling beyond [^\n], so the earliest 'due' wins whatever it is attached to (check.mjs:15); overlapping rules ('submit' feeds both deadline and submission, 'certif' matches 'certified check'); no negation handling; 'due' and 'question' are bare substrings ('overdue', 'due diligence'); the score is a percentage of keywords found, presented as a large green-styled metric (index.html:50) although its meaning is not monotone with readiness (more requirements found = higher score, negated ones too). Acceptable JS, weak as a text-extraction design.
evidence.claims: Checked against files and the vendor's page. Backed: disclaimer and no-SLA on all three pages (page.test.mjs, vs-govwin.test.mjs); no upload (index.html has no network code); not-affiliated note; no invented GovWin price ($ figures asserted absent). GovWin identity claims (Deltek product; opportunity discovery and forecasting, competitor tracking, SLED coverage, account-based) are backed by https://www.deltek.com/products/govwin/ fetched 2026-11-12 (scratchpad govwin.txt: 'federal, SLED, and AEC firms', 'Find Leads Years Before They Drop', 'get there before competitors do'). Not backed / contradicted: vs-govwin.html:54 and its JSON-LD (line 11) say reading one solicitation's bond, insurance and deadline requirements 'is not that platform's job', but Deltek's page says GovWin IQ helps teams 'make go/no-go decisions based on evidence' and that 'Dela AI builds on that foundation to surface opportunities, summarize documents, and score lead fit'; vs-govwin.html:33 says GovWin's feature list is 'not reachable from this session' (it was reachable today, so the page's comparison is unverified rather than unverifiable); vs-govwin.html:48 'Most public-sector contractors get different value from each' has no source; vs-govwin.html:63 says 'We count anonymous feature events locally' but the page has no counting script; index.html:9/13 FAQ says patterns match 'within 100 characters of a match' (the 100 characters are the evidence tail, not a matching window); llms.txt:5 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' is boilerplate that does not describe a text checker. The index FAQ is honest that green means a phrase was found, not met.
evidence.fitness: Walked the bid/no-bid job for a small contractor with a federal construction solicitation (SF 1442-style excerpt with FAR 52.228-1, 52.228-15, set-aside, SAM, site visit, amendments, Davis-Bacon) and a UK ITT. The tool returns 57% for both and misses the bid guarantee (unless a performance/payment bond is also mentioned), insurance, licensing and submission channel on the federal text and the bond-less licence and e-tendering channel on the UK text. Set-aside eligibility, SAM/UEI registration, bid acceptance period, liquidated damages, prevailing wage and DBE goals, which a capture manager checks at the same gate, are not signals at all. A bidder who trusts 'Found: bond' or the deadline excerpt can be misled (negations, question deadline shown as submission deadline). Usable only as a reminder list; the static checklist on should-i-bid-on-this-tender.html is more useful than the tool's output.
evidence.domain: Compared with Shipley Associates bid/no-bid practice and the APMP Body of Knowledge bid/no-bid gate (customer relationship, competitive position, ability to perform, probability of win, strategic fit, cost to bid, alongside responsiveness and compliance) and with FAR vocabulary (14.207 pre-bid conference, 15.201 preproposal conference, 28.101 bid guarantees, 52.214-3 amendments, 52.204-7 SAM, Part 19 set-asides). should-i-bid-on-this-tender.html:30 states 'The go/no-go is a paperwork decision, and it is answerable in ten minutes'; a capture manager would accept 'paperwork can make it a no-go' but not that the decision is paperwork alone. The responsiveness checklist on that page is sound in substance (two deadlines, bonding as a surety relationship, additional insured, unacknowledged addenda, wrong channel). The checker does not implement that checklist's distinctions: it does not separate the two deadlines, does not read amounts or limits, and does not know FAR's terms for the items FAR itself makes disqualifying.

defects.what: Bond rule misses FAR's own term: '52.228-1 Bid Guarantee ... not less than 20 percent of the bid price' and state 'bid security ... surety bond' both report bond Not found, although a missing bid guarantee generally makes a bid nonresponsive (FAR 28.101-4).

Deadline evidence is the first 'due' anywhere: when the question cut-off precedes the offer due date, the question date is shown under 'Find and verify the submission deadline' ('Questions are due by 2 January' over 'Proposals are due 20 January'); 'due diligence' and 'overdue' also count.

vs-govwin page says reading a solicitation's own bond, insurance and deadline requirements is 'not that platform's job'; Deltek's GovWin IQ page (fetched 2026-11-12) says it supports 'go/no-go decisions based on evidence' and that Dela AI will 'summarize documents, and score lead fit'. A comparative claim about a named competitor that its vendor page contradicts.
Negated requirements are reported as found ('No bid bond is required ... No license is required' -> 4 signals Found, score 57), and the score rises with them.

Site-visit signal misses FAR 'preproposal conference' and 'mandatory site inspection'; questions signal misses FAR 'amendments'; certification misses UK 'licence' and 'licensure'; submission misses 'sealed bids', 'delivered to', 'e-tendering'; deadline misses 'received until'; insurance misses 'additional insured'.
4 of 6 seeded mutations survive: no test of a partial score, of 'closing date', of 'addenda', or of the all-found warning text; no test of a FAR term, a negation or deadline selection.

Bid/no-bid scope gap: no signal for set-aside eligibility (FAR Part 19), SAM/UEI registration (52.204-7), bid acceptance period, liquidated damages, prevailing wage or DBE goals, and the guide page presents go/no-go as a paperwork decision only, departing from Shipley/APMP bid/no-bid criteria.

vs-govwin footer claims 'We count anonymous feature events locally' but the page has no counting code; line 33 says GovWin's feature list is 'not reachable from this session' though the vendor page is reachable; line 48 'Most public-sector contractors' is unsourced.

llms.txt says 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' (calculator boilerplate) for a text checker; index FAQ says patterns match 'within 100 characters of a match' when 100 characters is only the evidence tail.

verdict: Does not meet the bar (correctness 1, verification 1, claims 2; median 1); finished (completeness 3: it does the small set of things it lists, and the pages are served). The checker is seven first-match keyword regexes. On standard solicitation wording it is wrong where it matters most: a FAR 52.228-1 'bid guarantee' or a state 'bid security' clause is 'Not found' under bond, a question cut-off listed before the offer due date is shown as the submission deadline, 'No bid bond is required' counts as a found bond, FAR 'preproposal conference' and 'amendments' are missed, and decoy text with no requirements scores 71%. Four of six seeded mutations left all 16 tests green. The GovWin comparison is right about what GovWin IQ is, but its claim that reading a solicitation's requirements is not GovWin's job is contradicted by Deltek's own page (go/no-go support, Dela AI document summaries). A capture or bid manager would keep the guide page's checklist and not rely on the tool's output.
